utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, could you call the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Registrar. Today, Tuesday, the 15th of April, 2008. I would like to greet the Prosecution, Mr. Seselj, and everyone else assisting us. Very briefly, as we are waiting to call the witness into the courtroom, there is an issue, or rather, two issues I would like to address, two administrative issues. The first issue concerns Mr. Seselj. In May, we will be hearing the expert witness Riedlmayer. When this witness appears -- as this witness will be appearing, Mr. Seselj, the Chamber would like to know whether you have any additional written submissions. And if that is the case, you have one week at your disposal to provide the Chamber with these written submissions. I should also point out that the expert witness should be testifying on the 20th of May, 2008. You were informed of this fact on the 2nd of April. So if you and your assistants have any additional written submissions that you would like to provide us with that concern the expert report, you have one week at your disposal to provide us with such submissions. That is what I wanted to tell you. It's not necessary to debate the issue, which is a very simple one. So if there are any comments you would like to make, to do so. If you would like to take the floor, do so very briefly, because we have a witness who is waiting to be called into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, Your Honour, I provided a written submission in good time, and I said that I was contesting the expert and his expert report. I was contesting his qualifications. There's nothing new I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I take note of what you've said. And the second issue I would like to deal with very briefly is the following subject: The Prosecution has prepared the 600 binders, pursuant to Rule 68. Mr. Seselj has these binders at his disposal, but the deputy chief of the Detention Unit has said that we should send these -- we shouldn't send these binders before the 22nd of April, given the fact that work is ongoing. Mr. Mundis, on the 22nd of April, I presume that you will provide Mr. Seselj with these 600 binders. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, and everyone in and around the courtroom. My understanding is some of the binders went previously. The remaining binders are -- there's a second group of binders ready to go. We will hold off on that until they're ready at the Detention Unit. And there is a third category of binders from this material that is yet to be done, but I don't expect it would be ready before the 22nd of April in any event. We will not disclose any of that material until the Detention Unit informs us that they're ready to receive it for the simple practical and logistical reasons indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. They will have to put these binders in a cell that Mr. Seselj will have access to, because I believe that the binders will take up several shelves. So as of the 22nd of April, Mr. Seselj, you will have all this material at your disposal. As far as the witness who will be appearing is concerned, he will have protective measures. We will lower the blinds. We'll now call the witness into the courtroom. The Prosecution has three hours and Mr. Seselj has three hours for the cross-examination of the witness, too. Let's lower the blinds, then. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before the witness is brought into the courtroom, I did want to raise one issue concerning the witness with the Trial Chamber and Dr. Seselj. I would ask to do that in private session, before the witness comes into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Private session, then. Let's go into private session, and we'll lower the blinds at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th day of April, 2008, at 2.45 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
